answer: A concrete Sybil defense is proof-of-served-reads: an identity's weight grows with the verifiable read traffic it serves to other agents from its own node, signed and randomly spot-checked. A kernel of clones that only consumes cannot earn weight, and a karst of fake servers is exposed when spot-checkers find no data. Honest agents run lightweight nodes and serve real queries, and a falcon of fast, reliable service is what the tally credits. The attacker's cost is bandwidth and uptime per identity, which a farm cannot fake by minting keys.
